plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole avenues turn lavender-blue when jacarandas flower. Trumpet-shaped blossoms cover the branches and then fall to carpet the pavements in violet. Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of these spring displays.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late September to November, usually at its peak in October
plants.funFact: Jacaranda is native to South America, but it has become a symbol of spring in Pretoria, where thousands of the trees line the streets.

plants.name: Cyclamen hederifolium
plants.description: Small, swept-back pink flowers rise on slender stems from bare woodland soil. The ivy-shaped, silver-marbled leaves follow, and they carpet the ground through winter. It is a cheerful, tough plant for shady corners.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, from about October into November or early December in cultivation
plants.location: Temperate gardens of the UK and Ireland, and woodlands across southern Europe where it is native (Northern Hemisphere autumn)
plants.funFact: The plant's tuber can live for decades and keeps growing larger. Over time it can produce dozens of flowers in one season.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub opens its delicate, often lightly scented blooms as autumn cools. Its petals open flat to show golden stamens. They brighten the garden when most other plants are winding down.
plants.location: Temperate gardens in the UK and Europe, and native to Japan (Northern Hemisphere autumn)
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellias bloom earlier than their showier cousin, Camellia japonica. The two are related, but japonica flowers in late winter and spring.
